dialog_window.text: Sometimes practice seems pointless. One doesn't get the quick adreneline hits of progress one gets with coding.
Coding provides a tight, verifiable feedback loop. Practice, by contrast, lacks a compiler to tell you immediately if you've made progress.

Please monitor the PV controller every hour using the following procedure (this replaces
   any prior PV check rules):                                                             
   
  InfluxDB 1.8 lives at http://192.168.68.56:8086, database pv. Series: measurements      
  voltage and current, each tagged sys=pv, subsys=battery, subsys2=input|output. Field
  name is value (default; if a query returns nothing where data should exist, that's the  
  first thing to confirm).                                  

  Use fetch_text for the health check: GET /query?db=pv&q= with this query URL-encoded:   
  SELECT last("value"), time FROM "voltage" WHERE time > now() - 20m GROUP BY *
                                                                                          
  Important: do NOT compare time_iso fields client-side. InfluxDB returns timestamps in   
  UTC (Z suffix); the prompt-supplied clock is local time. Server-side filtering via now()
   avoids the timezone mismatch entirely.                                                 
                                                            
  Response shape: results[0].series is an array. If non-empty, you have one entry per tag 
  combination (battery input and battery output); each entry's values[0] is [time_iso,
  last_value] within the last 20 minutes — fresh by definition.                           
                                                            
  Battery is 48 V nominal. Healthy criteria:                                              
  - Response received from /query (no network/server failure).
  - results[0].series is non-empty (data is fresh by the WHERE clause).                   
  - Each voltage value is between 51.5 V and 57.5 V inclusive.
                                                                                          
  Flag any of:
  - No response (controller crash, server down, or network partition).                    
  - results[0].series missing or empty (data is stale — older than 10 minutes — by
  InfluxDB's own clock).                                                                  
  - Voltage < 51.5 V (battery low; charging fault or excessive load).
  - Voltage > 57.5 V (overcharge; charge controller fault).                               
                                                                                          
  Current readings (input and output) are informational only, not flagged. Apply the same
  checks to both voltage series — they should be near-equal at any moment since they      
  measure the same physical battery.                        

  Silent on healthy for autonomous checks; on manual checks always report raw input/output
   voltage values regardless of status.
